title: Service Discovery and Overlay Networking
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose and key terms of service discovery and overlay networking.
Choose and interpret a suitable Docker example connected to service discovery and overlay networking.
Predict an expected result and verify it using observable evidence in a controlled environment.

content.intro: This lesson covers Service Discovery and Overlay Networking. You will connect the named subtopics from the supplied Docker curriculum to a small, observable example. Work through the visual first, then use the example to form a prediction and check it against the actual behavior.
content.why_it_matters: A container network defines how services can discover and reach one another. User-defined bridge networks provide name-based discovery on one host; published ports expose a selected container port through the host, and overlay networking is for multi-host use such as Swarm. Restrict exposure to the services that need it. Learning service discovery and overlay networking helps you make deployment behavior explicit and repeatable instead of relying on a command that happened to work on one machine.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming that a successful start means the application is ready.
common_mistakes.why: A container can start while its dependent service is unavailable or the application is failing after startup.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect health/status and logs; add a meaningful health check or retry strategy where appropriate.

common_mistakes.problem: Keeping required data only in the container writable layer.
common_mistakes.why: Replacing the container can discard that layer and its application state.
common_mistakes.fix: Select a named volume or an external storage system, then rehearse a restore.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a command without checking context, target, or permissions.
common_mistakes.why: Docker commands affect the active endpoint and can change host resources or publish services.
common_mistakes.fix: Check `docker context show`, use an isolated lab, make the smallest change, and verify the resulting state.
